messages.content: Return exact JSON only. No markdown. Generate reversible log extraction functions.

You are a verifier-repair agent for OpenStack log compression.
Repair exactly one rejected reversible extraction function.
Return exact JSON only: {"functions": [ ... ]}.

Goal:
- Keep the original semantic intent when possible.
- Make the function pass a strict byte-exact verifier.
- Do not add dataset-specific constants beyond what appears in the examples and failed regex.
- Prefer the smallest safe repair: fix class/value_type, regex boundary, replacement, or python_exec code.
Repair category: executed_counterexample.
The verifier executed your program and supplies an actual failing input,
stored record, reconstructed text or exception below. Fix only program.code.
Keep regex, replacement, class, value_type, context and semantic intent unchanged.
Do not evade the failure by narrowing coverage to examples or storing raw text
instead of the intended number. Preserve every display byte via exact arithmetic
and the permitted layout. Do not assume floating-point scaling is exact.
forward receives all regex capture groups, or [whole_match] when there are none.
Available globals: abs, datetime, float, int, len, max, min, round, str, timedelta.
Imports and external state are forbidden. Return an empty list if unrepairable.

Required function schema:
{
  "tag": "short_name",
  "meaning": "short meaning",
  "class": "class_1_composed_numeric | class_2_formatted_numeric | class_3_common_variable",
  "value_type": "numeric | string",
  "target_role": "log_timestamp | ordinary_value",
  "context": null,
  "regex": "Python regex with explicit capture groups",
  "replacement": "template containing {placeholder} and any needed {groupN}",
  "program": {
    "op": "python_exec",
    "code": "def forward(groups):\n    ...\n\ndef inverse(record):\n    ..."
  }
}

Python execution contract:
- forward(groups) receives the captured value groups selected by the compiler.
- It returns {'stored': [...], 'layout': [...]}.
- inverse(record) reconstructs exactly the placeholder text from record['stored'] and record['layout'].
- For raw variables, use this executable pattern:
  def forward(groups):
      return {'stored': [groups[0]], 'layout': []}
  def inverse(record):
      return str(record['stored'][0])
- For numeric variables, store int values, not strings.
- Preserve exact spaces by capturing them as ( +) and either keeping them as {groupN} in replacement or storing layout.
- When repairing context, replace null with {"code": "def project_context(line, groups): ..."}; the function returns the actual context value or None.
